newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Briefing - Apr22.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Briefing - Apr22.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Brand-name Products, Consumer Trends and Media
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

BONN - The German government has enlisted a clutch of top athletes for this year's anti-drug publicity campaign, says federal drug commissioner, Eduard Lintner. Participants will include Olympic medallist skier Katja Seizinger, soccer star Oliver Bierhoff and Formula-1 driver Michael Schumacher. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Advertising agency WOB will join Lahmeyer AG in its stock market debut, which Lahmeyer hopes will boost its value as a management holding. The Lahmeyer Group includes Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG, SAG and Maquet AG. (Horizont)
MEDIA:

BONN - Deutsche Telekom chairman Ron Sommer, Bertelsmann chief Mark Woessner and Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch will meet top executives and state politicians for a German media summit next month, industry sources say. The high-level conference is a last-ditch bid to break a deadlock over the expansion of German cable television networks and the introduction of broadscale digital TV programming, which industry squabbling has held up for nearly two years. (Reuter)

BUDAPEST - Bertlesmann AG & Pearson Plc are involved in a joint venture bid for a Hungarian television channel, Hungarian telecommunications company Matav says. Matav says CLT-UFA, which is 50 percent owned by Bertelsmann, along with Matav, Pearson and Raiffeisen Unicbank have formed a joint venture company called M-RTL to bid for the channel. The joint venture is headed by CLT-UFA, which owns 49 percent of the new company.(Reuter)

MUNICH - Germany's second largest trade publishing group Weka says it plans to spend more than a billion marks ($585 million) before the end of the millennium to buy additional companies. The group said its turnover jumped 10 percent in 1996 to 680 million marks. (Reuter)

STUTTGART - The administrative board of Sueddeutscher Rundfunk (SDR) has called for changes in the just-ratified merger contract between SDR and Suedwestfunk (SWF). The broadcasting and administrative boards of SDR have approved the merger, but criticise some of its provisions. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & CONSUMER TRENDS:

BONN - Two of phone giant Deutsche Telekom AG's main rivals filed regulatory complaints with the government, saying the former monopoly was using its market dominance to prevent fair competition. (Reuter)

BONN - Germans, worried about their country's struggling economy and their own health, are cutting down on their beloved beer and switching to alcohol-free drinks, German brewers say. The German Brewers' Association (DBB) President Michael Dietzsch said annual per capita beer consumption dropped by 4.2 litres to 131.7 litres in 1996 and German beer production fell over 200 million litres to 11.4 billion litres. (Reuter)

BASLE - Swiss life sciences group Novartis AG says it will transfer its information technology activities into a joint venture that will be majority-owned by U.S. computer firm IBM. Later the venture will become an independent business unit of IBM, Novartis says. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - H.I.S. Sportswear AG is bringing the first German jeans company to stock exchanges in Frankfurt and Munich, says H.I.S. chairman Milan Danek. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Formerly freelance art director Regina Diedenhofen has signed on with BMZ FCA in Duesseldorf as deputy creative managing director. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Kurt Filip will take over as managing director of media agency Equmedia, a unit of Leo Burnett and DMB&B, says agency Michael Conrad & Leo Burnett (MC&LB). (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - The editor-in-chief of Zurich newspaper Tages-Anzeiger Roger de Weck has unexpectedly announced he is leaving his post. He cited cutbacks at the publication as leading to his stepping down. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)
